parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: Iron forms complex ions with the monodentate ligand, $\text{CN}^-$.
parts.text:
Complex ion **A** contains one $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ion and six $\text{CN}^-$ ligands.

Complex ion **B** contains one $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ion and six $\text{CN}^-$ ligands.

State the formulae of these two complex ions. Include the overall charge of each complex ion.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why a solution containing complex ion **A** and a solution containing complex ion **B** are different colours.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
In complex ion **A**, the carbon atom of each $\text{CN}^-$ ligand bonds to the $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ion.

State the type of bonding involved.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Complex ions have different geometries.

Complex ion **A** is octahedral.

$\text{Ag}^+$ ions form a linear complex with ammonia.

Ni atoms form a tetrahedral complex with carbon monoxide molecules. The carbon atom in the monodentate carbon monoxide ligand bonds to the nickel atom.

$\text{Pd}^{2+}$ ions form a square planar complex with chloride ions.

Complete Fig. 6.1 to show the geometry of each of these four ions, using three-dimensional bonds where necessary. Label **one** bond angle on each complex ion.
